subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should Birdclaw make third-party passive-capture files a core ingestion source, and if so should the first supported contract be limited to Scrollmark canonical bundle v1?
rationale: The feature aligns with the vision, but accepting external schemas and defining source identity, account attribution, completeness, and compatibility policy are durable product choices that automation should not make.

options.title: Scrollmark v1 first
options.body: Adopt only the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially, with explicit provenance and conservative partial-membership semantics.

options.title: Multi-format first release
options.body: Support Scrollmark legacy exports and twitter-web-exporter alongside the canonical bundle, accepting a larger compatibility and fixture burden.

options.title: Keep current sources only
options.body: Continue supporting official archives, Birdclaw backups, and live transports without establishing a third-party capture contract.

recommendation.title: Scrollmark v1 first
recommendation.body: Adopt only the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially, with explicit provenance and conservative partial-membership semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository vision and central canonical-storage history provide the strongest available ownership signal for this ingestion-boundary decision.
